memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Build an altar of acacia wood, three cubits high; it is to be square, five cubits long and five cubits wide. Make a horn at each of the four corners, so that the horns and the altar are of one piece, and overlay the altar with bronze." - Exodus 27:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Having described the beautiful inner rooms, God now turns to what stood in the open courtyard: the altar of burnt offering. This was the first thing anyone entering the tabernacle would meet. Before the lampstand, before the table, before the ark — the altar. You could not get to God's presence without first passing the place of sacrifice.

That order is not accidental. It preached the same sermon every day: approach to God begins with atonement. No worshipper could stroll past the altar and head straight for the holy things. Sin had to be dealt with first, and it was dealt with by death — a life given in place of the guilty.

This is why the cross stands at the very centre of the Christian faith. We do not come to God through our sincerity, our good record, or our religious effort. We come through a sacrifice made on our behalf. Jesus is our altar and our offering, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29). Everything else in the Christian life — worship, service, growth, joy — flows from that starting point. If you find your faith drifting into mere self-improvement, come back to the altar. That is where the way in begins.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I trying to approach God through my own effort rather than Christ's sacrifice?
Does the cross remain at the centre of my faith, or has it drifted to the edges?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I cannot come to You by my own goodness. Thank You for Jesus, my sacrifice and my way in. Keep the cross at the very centre of my life and my faith. Amen.
